decisions.quote: The optimal cut-off scores identified in the current study reflect the same results configured by the prior study. LAY SUMMARY: ADOS-2 Toddler Module has been widely used for the ASD assessment, but there have been limited research on its clinical validity. This study is the first replication of the ADOS-2 Toddler Module with a large independent sample. We examined alignment of the ADOS-2 Toddler Module classification with clinicians' determination of ASD, with assessing cut-off scores, and confirmed the clinical validity of ADOS-2 Toddler Module. Cut-off scores of ADOS-2 Toddler Module cited in the manual yielded best clinical utility for diagnosing ASD in toddlers.
decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files are absent for this request. The article body is unavailable; the source text contains only the abstract, lay summary, and a single reference-list excerpt for Luyster et al. (2009) (DOI 10.1007/s10803-009-0746-z). While the abstract states that the optimal cut-off scores reflect 'the same results configured by the prior study', the lay summary states that 'Cut-off scores of ADOS-2 Toddler Module cited in the manual yielded best clinical utility for diagnosing ASD in toddlers', which corresponds to shipped row input_row_index 143 (Lord et al., 2012, 'Autism diagnostic observation schedule--2nd edition (ADOS-2)'). Without the article body, the available evidence does not settle whether 'the prior study' refers to Luyster et al. (2009) or whether Luyster et al. (2009) and the ADOS-2 manual in shipped row 143 represent alternate reports of the same Toddler Module cut-off configuration rather than an omitted independent original study.
